data.narrative:
Cover operates in Housing & Construction at the Series B stage, having raised $100M+ to date. The valuation comp universe consists of four private peers in adjacent frontier-tech construction segments—Plantd Materials, Cuby Technologies, Somos, and Charge Robotics—with no direct public comparables available for triangulation.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach given data constraints. Using $100M in total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B-to-later-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $190M. This method anchors on the assumption that Cover's capital raise reflects investor conviction proportional to enterprise value at entry.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single methodological pillar, supports a valuation range of $162M (low) to $218M (high), with $190M as the median point. Key uncertainties include the absence of public market comparables, limiting cross-sector benchmarking; reliance on a single progression method without revenue multiple or precedent transaction validation; and the private comp set's limited granularity on revenue multiples or growth rates. A fuller valuation would benefit from revenue data, unit economics, and documented exit multiples among the peer group.
